problems: stop 1 card 4, answer 2: copies a Prep line word for word

explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). That means he won't lack a single thing he needs. When the Shepherd is on duty, the sheep are fully covered.
Not earn, friend. Sheep do not clock in for a shift to buy their grass. David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). He lacks nothing because the Shepherd provides it all.
Not lose, baker. David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). "Want" here means going without. With the LORD watching over him, he will lack nothing.
Spot on, baker. Green grass to lie down in and quiet waters to drink from mean the sheep is not running for its life (Psalm 23:2). It is totally calm, totally fed, and totally at peace.
No hustle here, friend. David says the LORD makes him lie down in green pastures and leads him beside quiet waters (Psalm 23:2). That is a picture of sweet rest and deep peace.
Not danger, baker. A sheep does not take a nap by quiet water if wolves are circling nearby (Psalm 23:2). This is a picture of complete safety and rest.
That is it, friend. David says, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). The LORD does not just fill the stomach with grass; He brings fresh life right back to David on the inside.
Not tests, baker. David says, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). When life wears a person thin, the Shepherd rebuilds and refreshes them from the inside out.
Not weighs, friend. David says, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). The Good Shepherd brings healing and new life to the soul that needs rest.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. David says, "He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). A shepherd's reputation is tied to how his sheep walk, and the LORD leads with total faithfulness.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His flock
explanations.explanation: Not for the flock, friend. David says, "He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). The Shepherd's own faithful name is on the line.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His land
explanations.explanation: Not for the land, baker. David writes that the LORD guides him "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). The LORD leads rightly because of who He is.

explanations.answer: Because the LORD is with him
explanations.explanation: That is the heart of it, baker. David says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). The valley is dark, but the Shepherd's presence changes everything.
Not because David is tough, friend. Sheep are not famous for fighting off dark valleys all by themselves. David says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4).
Not because of a short trip, baker. The valley might be long and deep, but David says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). It is the Shepherd's company that banishes the fear.

True it is, friend. David says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" (Psalm 23:4). The rod drives off wild beasts and the staff pulls a wandering sheep out of a ditch. In the Shepherd's hands, those tools mean safety.
It is actually true, baker. David says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" (Psalm 23:4). To a sheep in a dark valley, seeing the Shepherd hold tools to protect and guide is pure comfort.
You got it, baker. David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). The Shepherd turns into a generous Host who lays out a grand feast.
Not a tent, friend. David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). It is a full feast laid out for an honored guest.
Not a bed, baker. David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). The LORD invites David to sit down and dine as His guest.

Actually false, baker. David does not say he is hidden in a bunker far away. He says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). They have to watch the LORD treat him like royalty.

Right you are, friend. David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). The enemies are right there watching, but they cannot touch the guest at the LORD's table.
Spot on, friend. David says, "You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows" (Psalm 23:5). That cup is not barely half-full; the LORD pours out blessing until it runs right over the rim.
Not clumsy, baker. An overflowing cup is not a spill on the carpet. It means the Host is so generous that David has more than enough (Psalm 23:5).
No rush at all, friend. In Bible times, pouring until the drink spills over meant the guest was welcome to stay and enjoy boundless abundance (Psalm 23:5).
That is the pair, baker. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life" (Psalm 23:6). Those two faithful blessings trail right behind him wherever he goes.
Not wealth and honor, friend. David looks behind him and sees something far sweeter: "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life" (Psalm 23:6).
Not strength and wisdom, baker. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life" (Psalm 23:6). God's own goodness and steadfast love stick with him every single day.

explanations.answer: In the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: You nailed it, baker. David finishes his song saying, "and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). From green pastures to the valley, and all the way home to stay with the LORD forever.
Not Hebron, friend. David lived in cities as king, but for eternity he has a better home in mind. He says, "and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6).
Not just the land, baker. David aims all the way up. He closes his song with: "and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6).
